title: Read ee and ea
goal: Use a taught spelling pattern to attempt a word, check its pronunciation and connect it with meaning.
cue: Read ee in see as a unit. The ea in tea has the same vowel in this example. Not every ea word uses /i/; bread uses a different vowel.
spelling: ee commonly represents /i/. ea often does too, but compare tea with bread when you meet new words.
task: Mark ee in tree and ea in leaf. Blend each word, listen and decide whether your first attempt fits.
story: A green leaf is on a tree. Ben can see it.

articulation.label: see
articulation.alt: see: /s/ → /i/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /s/: Make a narrow gap near the ridge; let air flow.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: tree
articulation.alt: tree: /t/ → /r/ → /i/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
/r/: Bunch the tongue; leave space at the ridge.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: tea
articulation.alt: tea: /t/ → /i/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: leaf
articulation.alt: leaf: /l/ → /i/ → /f/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /l/: Tip at the ridge; air passes round the sides.
/f/: Upper teeth lightly touch the lower lip.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

sections: a large plant with a trunk. There is a tall tree beside our house.

A small round green seed eaten as a vegetable. There is a pea on my plate.
put food in your mouth and swallow it. Puck eats breakfast at home.
